notes: Matched-pairs leukaemia survival trial, 21 pairs of two patients; documented survreg(Surv(time, cens) ~ factor(pair) + treat, exponential), rendered as random effects on the pair block (Census blocked-design rule). Barley field trial, 6 locations (Loc block) x 5 varieties; yields stored wide for 1931 (Y1) and 1932 (Y2); documented aov(cbind(Y1,Y2) ~ Loc + Var) and aov((Y1+Y2)/2 ~ Var + Loc), Loc the block. Speed-of-light measurements, five experiments (Expt) of 20 consecutive runs each; V&R MASS examine between-experiment variation of Speed by experiment, the help page states no model. Run is the within-experiment run index (ignore).

formula: Length ~ asymptotic regression alpha[Strip] + beta*rho^Conc on calcium chloride concentration (Conc); strip-specific asymptote
notes: NONLINEAR: V&R MASS fit nls(log(Length) ~ alpha[Strip] + beta*rho^Conc) over 21 rat heart-muscle strips with strip-specific asymptotes; Strip is the grouping, Conc the covariate, response Length fitted on log(Length).

Snijders & Bosker running example, 2287 eighth-grade pupils in 132 classes; documented nlme::lme(lang ~ IQ*COMB + IQave + SES, random = ~ IQ | class). IQ centred within class; IQave is the class-mean of IQ (derived, not a table column); GS (class size) unused; random slope on IQ.

Classical NPK pea factorial on 6 blocks; documented aov(yield ~ block + N*P*K), block rendered as random (Census blocked-design rule). The fractional design confounds the N:P:K interaction with blocks; the reduced aov(yield ~ block + N + K) is a fixed-effects simplification (same model).

Split-plot field trial: 6 blocks (B), 3 varieties (V) on main plots, 4 nitrogen levels (N) on sub-plots; documented aov(Y ~ Nf*V + Error(B/V)), where B/V gives the block B and whole-plot B:V error strata. Nf is N as an ordered factor.

notes: Prater's petrol refinery data, 10 crude-oil samples (No); documented nlme::lme(Y ~ SG + VP + V10 + EP, random = ~ 1 | No). SG, VP, V10 are constant within sample, EP varies; the reduced fixed = Y ~ V10 + EP is a nested simplification (same model).
